results.correct_value: About 2,400 ft (2,444 ft) of gain over 1.6 mi one way from the Upper Trailhead
results.evidence: WTA gives 2,444 ft of gain in the 1.6 miles from the upper trailhead to the summit (3.2 mi round trip). onX gives 2,418 ft over ~3.1 mi out-and-back, and another trip guide gives ~2,400 ft; USFS gives the upper trailhead at 3,500 ft and summit at 5,944 ft. Every field except partner_requirements already says 2,444 ft; the 3,200 ft figure is wrong.

patches.find: about 3,200 ft of gain over ~1.6 mi one way
patches.replace: about 2,400 ft of gain over ~1.6 mi one way

results.correct_value: Summit waypoint at 1.6 mi from the Upper Trailhead
results.evidence: The USFS upper-trailhead listing says the trail from the 3,500 ft upper trailhead reaches the summit in 1.6 miles; WTA likewise gives 1.6 miles to the summit (3.2 mi round trip). The row's approach, approach_variants, itinerary and dist_km all agree on ~1.6 mi; only the summit pin's 1.21 disagrees.

results.correct_value: Only a Northwest Forest Pass (or equivalent recreation pass) for parking at the upper trailhead; no entrance fee and no wilderness permit for this day climb
results.evidence: The USFS Trail #812 page says a valid Recreation Pass is required for day use at the upper trailhead and none at the lower one, with no entrance fee or permit named (this is national forest, not a park). WTA also lists only a Northwest Forest Pass. access.notes' 'standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit' is park boilerplate that contradicts permit, access.permit and access.rules.

patches.find: only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
patches.replace: the only charge is the Northwest Forest Pass (or equivalent recreation pass) for parking at the upper trailhead.
